sources.title: The Commercial Storage of Fruits, Vegetables, and Florist and Nursery Stocks
sources.authors_or_publisher: Edited by Kenneth C. Gross, Chien Yi Wang, and Mikal Saltveit; USDA Agricultural Research Service
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened and read the published PDF from USDA-ARS.
sources.locator: Chapter 'Precooling and Storage Facilities'; PDF pages 20–24, especially 'Initial Cooling Methods', 'Forced-Air Cooling', and 'Hydrocooling' (PDF p.20 lines 994–1053 and pp.22–23 lines 1060–1173 in web text view).
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Separates initial cooling from transport; says special facilities remove produce heat, highway trailers have insufficient airflow for dependable initial cooling, and forced-air performance depends on airflow, produce diameter, vents and internal packaging.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Commodity and package dependent. Forced air is broadly adaptable; hydrocooling needs products that tolerate water and water-resistant packaging; vacuum cooling is for rapid moisture-releasing crops; room cooling has exceptions including certain citrus and CA-stored apples. Avoid transferring numeric storage tables to unspecified produce.
sources.applicability: Supports asking about initial product condition and evaluating product-compatible preconditioning, ventilation and packaging before buying transport cooling.
sources.limitations: General handbook, not cooperative measurements, not a current product-specific specification, and not evidence of safety or a specific temperature limit.

sources.title: Protecting Perishable Foods During Transport by Truck or Rail
sources.authors_or_publisher: Jeffrey K. Brecht, Steven Sargent, Patrick E. Brecht, Jorge Saenz, and Leonard Rodowick; University of Florida IFAS Extension
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current web publication viewed 2026-10-10; page does not display a publication/revision date. Preface identifies it as a revision of Handbook 669 (last revised 1995), which revised the 1987 edition and superseded Handbook 105 first published in 1956 and revised in 1970.
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened the IFAS HTML publication and read its measurement, cargo and airflow sections.
sources.locator: Preface lines 130–136; section I 'Telematics' and 'Air Temperature vs. Product Temperature' lines 483–499; section II 'Temperature Recording and Tracking' lines 802–823; section III 'Type of Air Delivery System' lines 831–840.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Explains that air-space readings can change faster than product temperatures; recommends date/time plus documented logger location and gives three-position guidance for trailer/container mapping (front, center, rear). Describes air-delivery and package/stack effects.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Temperature and correct placement depend on cargo location, commodity, air-delivery type, package and loading. Three positions are transport-mapping guidance, not a universal minimum or placement prescription for a small insulated-crate route.
sources.applicability: Supports paired air/in-crate/product measurements, position labeling, route and load event records, and treating logger channels as different measurements.
sources.limitations: Extension handbook guidance, not an experiment on this vehicle or produce; it contains commodity guidance not used here to set any threshold. Food-safety sections are not used to infer safety.

sources.title: Identifying cooling heterogeneity during precooling and refrigerated trailer transport for the citrus supply chain by extensive temperature monitoring within full-scale experiments
sources.authors_or_publisher: Celine Verreydt, Emmanuel Cobbinah-Sam, Ana Mikler Celis, Martin Meckesheimer, Nikos Prountzos, Raphael Sacher, Elisabeth Tobler, and Thijs Defraeye; Food Control
sources.released_version_or_commit: Version of record published November 2024; volume 165, article 110672; DOI 10.1016/j.foodcont.2024.110672.
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened the Wageningen University & Research record and read its abstract and publication metadata.
sources.locator: Abstract and record metadata lines 25–37; article DOI and CC BY access links lines 34–52.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Measured air and fruit temperatures with 108 sensors in one Greece–Switzerland commercial citrus shipment and added rear-trailer measurements in 30 shipments; reports room-precooled fruit not uniformly at study target after 24 h and some middle-of-trailer reheating associated with insufficient pallet ventilation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Large refrigerated trailer, citrus, specific precooling and export route; the paper's setpoint is specific to this study. Air and fruit values are spatially variable.
sources.applicability: Shows why initial cooling, airflow, pallet/crate configuration and mapped positions should be part of the investigation.
sources.limitations: Not a short cooperative route, not the unspecified produce or insulated-crate system here, and does not establish a transferable temperature target.

sources.title: Thermal Management of Short-Range Distribution of Perishable Food Products Using Phase Change Materials in Packaging: Real-Time Field Data Acquisition
sources.authors_or_publisher: Martim Aguiar, Pedro Dinis Gaspar, and Pedro Dinho da Silva; Energies
sources.released_version_or_commit: Version of record, Energies 2023, 16, 5191; DOI 10.3390/en16135191; open CC BY.
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened the 13-page published PDF from the University of Beira Interior repository.
sources.locator: Methods pp.3–8 (crate/PCM, orange loading, van and sensors); results pp.9–11; conclusions p.11. Relevant web text lines 147–153, 219–256, 263–315, 383–386, 461–480, 683–705, 713–733.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Compared reusable PCM alveoli with empty alveoli in orange crates on a short delivery route; temperature/humidity sensors were in and near produce, sampled/transmitted every five minutes, with ambient and rear/front crate positions. The abstract reports less temperature variation with PCM; unload spikes were observed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Orange crates stored around 5 °C overnight, bespoke 600×400×90 mm PP crate, about 48 oranges per crate, PCM transition around 5–6 °C, insulated IVECO Daily van, winter run with refrigeration off, crates near right wall and rear door, mixed customer-order cargo. The abstract describes 8 h while methods list 08:00–14:05. Sensors measured surrounding air, not pulp; paper identifies PCM quantity/autonomy, route/crop/climate fit and reuse as open issues.
sources.applicability: Strong comparator for short-route PCM inserts, logging positions, stop/open events and passive package buffering.
sources.limitations: Single route/context with crate-air readings and no measured delivered-quality endpoint; no direct evidence for this crop, crate, weather, route, reefer status or economics.

sources.title: Artificial fruit for monitoring the thermal history of horticultural produce in the cold chain
sources.authors_or_publisher: Thijs Defraeye, Wentao Wu, Kevin Prawiranto, Giuseppino Fortunato, Shelley Kemp, Stefan Hartmann, Paul Cronje, Pieter Verboven, and Bart Nicolai; Journal of Food Engineering
sources.retrieval_operation: Searched and read the ScienceDirect article record/abstract after a direct page opening did not return content.
sources.locator: Abstract and introduction in the article record; verification comparison is between one artificial apple and ten real apples during cooling.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: A fruit-shaped, biomimetic thermal simulator contained its own logger; the prototype's apple cooling time was within 5% of ten real apples and was more representative than water-filled simulators, whose response differed by up to 16%. It can be packed at multiple cargo positions.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Validation was for an apple-like prototype during cooling, with a target-specific shell/filling and thermal response. A simulator must be matched to the crop and operation.
sources.applicability: A plausible measurement-placement alternative for later repeated core-like temperature mapping without relying on a loose top logger.
sources.limitations: Does not validate a simulator for unknown vegetables or an actual route. It estimates thermal history, not quality or safety.

sources.title: Heat and mass exchanging processes in a refrigerated truck body during multi-drop urban distribution of fresh herbs
sources.authors_or_publisher: Vladimir N. Kornienko; Revista San Gregorio
sources.released_version_or_commit: Published 2020-04-04; Vol. 1, No. 37, Special Edition March 2020; original research article.
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened the publisher article page and read abstract, issue/date and study description.
sources.locator: Publisher abstract lines 31–46; publication date and issue metadata lines 97–110.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Two-stage study in an 11 m³ refrigerated truck body with dill and parsley; measured air temperature, air velocity and humidity under different door-open durations and assessed herbs after transit/storage. Its abstract reports rapid air/moisture entry after opening.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Specific herb, vehicle and experimental sequence; a heat calculation used an empty body; the paper's microbiological results are not treated as safety evidence.
sources.applicability: Supports logging door/opening duration and route-stop events as covariates, not assuming a short spike means core temperature changed.
sources.limitations: A single specific truck/herb setup; not applicable for numeric thermal/quality/safety predictions for this case.

sources.title: Management of reusable plastic crates in fresh produce supply chains: A technical guide
sources.authors_or_publisher: Rosendo S. Rapusas and Rosa S. Rolle; FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened the FAO publication record and read the abstract/publication metadata.
sources.locator: Title, report number and publication metadata lines 2–24; scope and abstract lines 37–40.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Guide describes reusable-crate handling/storage, cleaning/sanitization protocols and a returnable-crate management/pooling model for supply-chain participants.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Applies to reusable plastic crate systems in horticultural chains; the cooperative’s container type and reuse cycle are unknown.
sources.applicability: Provides an implementation-history checklist for crate ownership, replacement, repair, cleaning and reuse when reconstructing packaging history.
sources.limitations: Not a thermal-performance test and not evidence the cooperative uses RPCs or a particular crate pool.

sources.title: Cooling efficiency and effectiveness of single-crate evaporative cooler for selected fresh produce
sources.authors_or_publisher: Ryan Anthony O. Lualhati and Dormita R. Del Carmen; Philippine Journal of Crop Science
sources.released_version_or_commit: August 2018; volume 43, issue 2, pp.47–55; repository record 5138.
sources.retrieval_operation: Opened the University of the Philippines Los Baños repository article record; full document is marked unavailable there, so only the abstract was read.
sources.locator: Abstract and issue metadata lines 26–39 and 40–58.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Tested a portable evaporative crate made by wrapping a plastic crate with duck cloth for selected lettuce, rambutan, bitter gourd and eggplant; reports cooling/quality effects in those tests.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Evaporative cooling depends on crop and ambient conditions, including evaporative potential; the available abstract does not provide enough local RH/route/start-temperature detail to transfer benefits.
sources.applicability: Screening lead for a non-powered option only if crop, climate, water access and handling conditions match.
sources.limitations: Full methods unavailable in the accessed repository record; not recommended or treated as a proven alternative for this cooperative.

sources.title: Evaporative cooling with a wet fabric blanket for non-refrigerated horticultural produce transport: An experimental study
sources.authors_or_publisher: Nattawut Chaomuang, Onrawee Laguerre, Suriyan Supapvanich, Denis Flick, and Steven Duret; Journal of Agriculture and Food Research
sources.released_version_or_commit: Version of record, volume 18 (December 2024), article 101339; DOI 10.1016/j.jafr.2024.101339; CC BY.
sources.retrieval_operation: Read the ScienceDirect search result/abstract and KMITL repository metadata, including study method and conditions; did not fetch supplemental data.
sources.locator: Abstract and methods summary: full-scale Thai cargo chamber; 29–30 °C and 70–73% RH; airflow 0.8–3.6 m/s; three-hour test; every-minute thermocouple/hygrometer readings; lettuce mass-loss comparison.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Evaluated a wet fabric blanket as a passive evaporative transport medium. The thermal surrogate load used hollow plastic balls; the abstract also reports lettuce mass-loss observations. Air temperature fell by about 3–4 °C under the studied condition.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Tropical fixed climate and simulated transport airflow; exact result depends on external humidity, airflow, water management, package/load and crop. Thermal surrogate is not actual produce core.
sources.applicability: A non-powered alternative to screen if local product, climate, airflow, water availability and handling match; include as a controlled pilot option only after baseline.
sources.limitations: One chamber experiment and lettuce mass-loss endpoint; no proof for cooperative route or unspecified crop; no safety inference.

sources.title: Full-scale experiments in forced-air precoolers for citrus fruit: Impact of packaging design and fruit size on cooling rate and heterogeneity
sources.authors_or_publisher: Wentao Wu, Philippe Häller, Paul Cronjé, and Thijs Defraeye; Biosystems Engineering
sources.released_version_or_commit: Version of record published May 2018; volume 169, pp.115–125; DOI 10.1016/j.biosystemseng.2018.02.003.
sources.retrieval_operation: Read the ScienceDirect search-result abstract; direct article-page open returned HTTP 403 at 2026-10-10T07:06:18Z. Read bibliographic/author metadata from the Empa-hosted accepted-manuscript search result at 2026-10-10T07:08:48Z; direct accepted-manuscript PDF open returned HTTP 403 at 2026-10-10T07:09:20Z. Full text was not accessed.
sources.locator: Search-result record, abstract and conclusion; study ran commercial forced-air precooling in a 40-pallet facility using Navel oranges, Nova mandarins and Eureka lemons, package/wrap conditions and high-resolution pallet sensors.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Full-scale commercial forced-air experiments found cooling heterogeneity mainly along airflow direction; wrapping slowed cooling and increased heterogeneity. Package/fruit-size comparisons showed cooling-rate differences up to 42% for particular citrus/package comparisons.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Specific commercial facility, citrus types, forced-air cooling and carton designs; differences depend on fruit size, airflow direction, package vents, wrapping and pallet stacking. This is pre-cooling evidence, not a short insulated-crate route test.
sources.applicability: Supports inspecting crate vents, liners/wrap, packing and air paths, and testing package changes under matched loads before claiming that insulation or ventilation helps.
sources.limitations: Citrus and a commercial forced-air precooler; search abstract only was read. Do not transfer its cooling rates to this route or crop.

sources.title: A phase change material (PCM) based passively cooled container for integrated road-rail cold chain transportation – An experimental study
sources.authors_or_publisher: Shanhu Tong, Binjian Nie, Zixiao Li, Chunhai Li, Boyang Zou, Lin Jiang, Yi Jin, and Yulong Ding; Applied Thermal Engineering
sources.released_version_or_commit: Version of record, August 2021, volume 195, article 117204; DOI 10.1016/j.applthermaleng.2021.117204.
sources.retrieval_operation: Read the ScienceDirect search-result article metadata and abstract; full article text was not accessed.
sources.locator: Publisher abstract and highlights: integrated road–rail refrigerated container with PCM cold-energy storage plates, separate charging facility, four types of fresh produce, monitored charging/discharge and product quality; article reports discharge duration up to 94.6 h.
sources.reported_behavior_or_method: Built and tested a PCM-based container with storage plates and a separate charging facility that charges the plates. Compared operation with diesel-powered refrigerated container and assessed four fresh fruit/vegetable types.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Vehicle-scale road–rail use and separately charged plates; four crops and long-distance conditions are mentioned but not specified in the accessible abstract. Claimed duration/cost/energy results belong to that setup only.
sources.applicability: Shows that passive thermal storage still depends on an upstream charging/conditioning operation and sufficient thermal capacity; useful background for recording conditioning labor/energy and autonomy.
sources.limitations: Abstract-only source access; vehicle-scale long road–rail implementation is not a small-route crate insert and no result is transferred to this case.
